disclaimer: Belfort is free, open-source software for learning and research. It is not investment advice or a recommendation to buy, sell or hold any security, and its authors are not SEBI-registered research analysts or investment advisers. Labels state whether fixed, published rules are met; they do not predict returns. Practice uses virtual points with no money value. Markets carry risk and you can lose money. Belfort never places orders.

home.h1: Research a stock before you risk money on it.
home.intro: Search any NSE company, or start from a screen. Each stock is checked against a fixed, published rule: which conditions hold, the main risk, the price that proves an idea wrong, and how many shares fit your risk limit. You make every decision.
intro.quote: Risk comes from not knowing what you’re doing.

nw.r1: A headline is one fact, not a forecast. Ask what changed and for whom.
nw.r2: Big moves on news often reverse. Your stop matters more than the story.
nw.r3: Check the date: old news is already in the price.

overview.explain: “Conditions met” needs every condition. A downtrend or a serious business concern gives “Rule excludes”. Anything else is “Partly met”. Chart patterns are not part of the rule.

rp.defaults: The default stop sits just under the lowest low of the last 20 sessions, and the target at twice the risk. Change both.
rp.intro: Belfort picks a real past chart at random and hides the company and the future. Plan a trade on what you can see: buy with a stop and target, or skip. Then watch the next 60 sessions play out. Many repetitions in an hour, instead of one result a month.
